title: should para dar consejos
short: You should rest. You shouldn't worry. Should I call? Should + verbo, sin to y sin -s.

story.title: Deberías…
story.text: Para dar un consejo usamos ==should== (deberías, debería). Es más suave que must: no es una orden, es una recomendación.

story.title: Igual para todos
story.text: ==should== + verbo base. Nunca cambia: sin -s, sin to y sin do.

story.title: Pedir consejo
story.text: Para pedir consejo, ==should== va delante del sujeto. Y es muy natural empezar con ==I think== o ==I don't think==.

examples.t: I think you should see a doctor.
examples.es: Creo que deberías ir al médico.

examples.t: I don't think you should go out.

story.title: Así en español, así en inglés
story.text: En español: «deberías» + infinitivo, y la persona va en el verbo. En inglés: sujeto + ==should== + verbo base, y should no cambia nunca.

examples.t: Deberías dormir más. → You should sleep more.

story.title: should, must, have to
story.text: ==should==: es buena idea. ==must / have to==: es obligatorio. Con should, la otra persona decide.

examples.t: You must wear a seat belt.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ You should to rest. ✅ You ==should rest==.
❌ She shoulds go. ✅ She ==should== go.
❌ Do I should call? ✅ ==Should I== call?
❌ He should goes. ✅ He should ==go==.

story.title: Truco: should suena «shud»
story.text: La l de should ==no se pronuncia==: suena «shud». Igual que could y would. Y shouldn't suena «shúdnt».

compare.es: En español damos consejos con «deberías / debería» + infinitivo o con «¿por qué no…?». La persona va en la terminación del verbo.
compare.target: En inglés usamos should + verbo base, igual para todas las personas: You should rest, She should rest. Negativa: shouldn't. Pregunta: Should I…? Sin to, sin -s y sin do.

errors.why: Después de should no va to.

errors.wrong: He should goes to the dentist.
errors.right: He should go to the dentist.
errors.why: Después de should, el verbo va en forma base.

errors.wrong: Do I should call the doctor?
errors.why: Should no usa do: va delante del sujeto.
La negativa es shouldn't, sin don't.

exercises.q: What ___ I do? My phone isn't working.
exercises.why: Para pedir consejo: What should I do?

exercises.q: It's cold. You ___ wear a coat.
exercises.why: Hace frío: es buena idea llevar abrigo.

exercises.q: You ___ carry heavy bags with a bad back.
exercises.why: Con dolor de espalda no es buena idea: shouldn't.

exercises.q: I think you ___ see a doctor.
exercises.es: Creo que deberías ir al médico.

exercises.q: You ___ watch TV so late. Go to sleep!
exercises.es: No deberías ver la tele tan tarde. ¡A dormir!

exercises.q: My grandson should ___ his homework now.
exercises.es: Mi nieto debería hacer los deberes ahora.

exercises.q: I don't think you ___ drive in this rain.
exercises.es: No creo que debas conducir con esta lluvia.
exercises.why: I don't think you should… = no creo que debas.

exercises.q: My friend should eats more vegetables.
exercises.why: Después de should, verbo base: eat (aunque sea my friend).

exercises.q: Do I should wear a jacket?
exercises.why: Should va delante: Should I…? (sin do).

answer: My friend should do more exercise.

exercises.answer: You should go to the doctor
alt: You should go to the doctor's

exercises.context: Tu amiga te dice que no duerme bien. Le das un consejo.
options: You shouldn't drink coffee at night.
You shouldn't to drink coffee at night.
exercises.answer: You shouldn't drink coffee at night.

exercises.context: No sabes qué regalarle a tu nieto. Le pides consejo a tu hijo.
options: What should I buy for him?
What I should buy for him?
exercises.answer: What should I buy for him?

exercises.context: Tu hijo trabaja demasiado y está estresado.
options: I think you should take a holiday.
I think you must to take a holiday.
I think you should taking a holiday.
exercises.answer: I think you should take a holiday.
exercises.why: I think you should + verbo base.

pairs: You should go to bed early.
